jump.heightTiles.label: Jump height
jump.heightTiles.note: MEASURED 3.91 character-heights from jumps.mov (large/held jump), x2.0 tiles per character. Confidence: soft, +/-15% from the character-height denominator. 2.6x the original plan guess of 3.0.

jump.timeToApexMs.label: Time to apex
jump.timeToApexMs.note: MEASURED 333ms, flat ground, camera-compensated. Confidence: solid. Identical for medium and held jumps, so this is the engine's rise time.

jump.fallGravityMultiplier.label: Fall gravity
jump.fallGravityMultiplier.note: MEASURED 1.00 from the small jump (rise 128ms = fall 128ms, perfectly symmetric). UNUSUAL - most 2D platformers use 1.5-2.5 because it feels better. This is a 1999 3D game; treat 1.0 as the reference's answer, not necessarily the right one. Most likely value to change by feel.

jump.releaseCutMultiplier.label: Tap-jump cut
jump.releaseCutMultiplier.note: DERIVED from measured tap:hold height ratio 1.18:3.91 = 0.30. Height scales with v^2, so velocity cut = sqrt(0.30) = 0.55.

jump.coyoteMs.label: Coyote time
jump.coyoteMs.note: GUESS. Raised from the plan's 100 because the design target is explicitly forgiving, not precision-demanding.

run.maxSpeedTilesPerSec.label: Run speed
run.maxSpeedTilesPerSec.note: GUESS - not measured. Genre convention plus the plan's original value. IF THE JUMP FEELS TOO VERTICAL, RAISE THIS rather than lowering jump height: height is measured, this is not. At 8.0 the full-airtime reach is 5.4 tiles against a 7.8 tile jump height.

run.timeToMaxSpeedMs.label: Accel to full run
run.timeToMaxSpeedMs.note: GUESS. Slightly slower than the plan's 120 to suit a momentum-forward feel.

swing.dampingPerSecond.label: Swing damping
swing.dampingPerSecond.note: PER SECOND, converted per-step at load. 0.74/sec = 0.995/step at 60Hz. Putting 0.995 in this key makes the vine near-frictionless and reads as weightless, not as a unit bug.

swing.releaseBoostMultiplier.label: Swing release boost
swing.releaseBoostMultiplier.note: GUESS, but constrained: the manual frames vine release as the wide-pit crossing tool, so a swing must out-range a jump. At current values max release is 24 tiles/sec = 3x run speed. If chained swings do not clearly beat jumping, raise this.

swing.grabRadiusTiles.label: Grab assist radius
swing.grabRadiusTiles.note: GUESS. First thing to raise if vine chaining feels like work - never change the pendulum physics instead.

swing.grabRadiusTouchMultiplier.label: Grab assist - touch bonus
swing.grabRadiusTouchMultiplier.note: Raise this on the phone, not the base radius, so desktop feel is not degraded to fix touch.

camera.deadzoneHeightTiles.label: Camera deadzone height
camera.deadzoneHeightTiles.note: GUESS, raised from the plan's 3.0. With a 7.8 tile jump a tight deadzone pans the camera on every hop. The original pans aggressively - 254px measured - which is exactly what made its footage hard to measure.

world.characterHeightTiles.label: Character height
world.characterHeightTiles.note: THE LOAD-BEARING ASSUMPTION. Every measured value from the reference is in character-heights, so this number scales all of them. At 2.0 the jump is 7.8 tiles; at 1.5 it would be 5.9; at 2.5 it would be 9.8. Change this first if the whole game feels wrongly scaled, and re-derive rather than patching individual values.
